faqs.question: How do I apply for admission at SZABIST Hyderabad?
faqs.answer: Admissions at SZABIST Hyderabad are announced for the Fall (August) and Spring (January) semesters. Check hyd.szabist.edu.pk for the current admission status and application form, or visit the Admission Office on the Ground Floor, State Life Building, Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

faqs.question: What are the admission requirements?
faqs.answer: For undergraduate programs you need Intermediate or A-Levels (with IBCC equivalence where applicable). For Masters and MS programs your last degree is required and is verified by HEC. PhD applicants need a GAT Subject score of at least 60%. Admission is based on the SZABIST admission test and interview. Specific requirements vary by program.

faqs.question: What is the admission deadline and when does the semester start?
faqs.answer: Deadlines are announced every semester on the SZABIST Hyderabad website and notice boards. The Fall semester begins in August, the Spring semester in January, and the Summer semester in June. Provisionally admitted students must submit their educational documents by 31st December.

faqs.question: Which programs are offered at SZABIST Hyderabad?
faqs.answer: SZABIST Hyderabad offers BBA, BS Computer Science (BSCS), BS Software Engineering (BSSE), BS Artificial Intelligence (BSAI), BS Accounting and Finance, BS Social Sciences, MBA, MS Computer Science, MS Management Sciences, and PhD programs. Offered programs may change, so confirm with the Admission Office.

faqs.question: Is there an admission test and how do I prepare?
faqs.answer: Yes, applicants take the SZABIST admission test and an interview. A sample test paper is available on the SZABIST Hyderabad website to help you prepare. Test dates are announced with each admission cycle.

faqs.question: How much is the tuition fee?
faqs.answer: Tuition fee depends on the program. As a guide, BBA, MBA and MS programs at SZABIST Hyderabad cost approximately Rs 135,000 per semester. Fees for BSCS, BSSE and other programs differ, so please confirm the exact amount for your program with the Admission Office or Finance Office. Student activity charges are about Rs 1,500 per semester.

faqs.question: What other charges do I pay at the time of admission?
faqs.answer: At admission you pay a one-time admission fee, which is non-refundable, and a security deposit, which is refunded after adjustment of any dues when you clear your degree. Examination, lab and student activity charges are also added to each semester's fee challan.

faqs.question: How do I pay my fees?
faqs.answer: Pay your fee challan at any Bank Al-Habib Limited branch by cash, banker's cheque or demand draft, or online through Bank Al-Habib Internet Banking or Mobile App. Other banks' mobile apps can also be used for direct credit to the account titled SZABIST Hyderabad Campus. After paying, upload a screenshot of the paid challan with your challan number, registration ID and payment date using the form given by the Finance Office.

faqs.question: Can I pay fees in installments?
faqs.answer: Fees are announced before each semester and must be paid by the announced deadline. For any installment arrangement or fee difficulty, contact the Finance Office on the Ground Floor, ext. 154. SZABIST also offers interest-free loans and scholarships for students who need financial support.

faqs.question: What happens if I pay my fee late?
faqs.answer: A late payment surcharge applies: 5% of outstanding semester dues if paid up to the end of the 4th week, 5% plus Rs 1,000 from the 5th to the 10th week, and 5% plus Rs 2,000 from the 11th week onward. Your ZabDesk account may also be closed until the fee is paid.

faqs.question: What is the fee refund policy?
faqs.answer: On admission withdrawal, 100% of tuition fee is refunded up to the 7th day after classes begin, and 50% from the 8th to the 14th day. There is no tuition refund from the 15th day. The admission fee is never refundable, while the security deposit is refunded if you have no dues.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available?
faqs.answer: Yes. SZABIST-funded scholarships include Need-Based, Merit-Based, Talent-Based, Board of Governors/Chancellor, and General scholarships. External scholarships include Sindh Education Endowment Fund, Chief Minister SZABIST Merit and Need-Based, USAID, Pakistan Education Endowment Fund and Sindh HEC Indigenous scholarships. Contact the Academics Department or the External Relations and Financial Assistance (ERFA) Department for details.

faqs.question: How does the need-based scholarship work?
faqs.answer: The Need-Based Scholarship covers one semester and can pay 100%, 75%, 50% or 25% of tuition. Both new and continuing students can apply if the maximum annual family income is below Rs 1,500,000. Continuing students also need a minimum CGPA of 2.5. It is not available for PhD students.

faqs.question: How does the merit-based scholarship work?
faqs.answer: From the second semester onward, the student with the highest semester GPA in a class who has at least 3.70 GPA and took a full course load gets a 25% fee waiver for the following semester. Transfer students, LLB, EMBA, MS and PhD students are not eligible, and the scholarship is renewable each semester based on performance.

faqs.question: Does SZABIST offer loans or study now pay later options?
faqs.answer: Yes. SZABIST supports students through Ihsan Trust's Qarz-e-Hasna interest-free loan, The Citizens Foundation financial assistance, and the EDUFI Study Now Pay Later program. Contact the External Relations and Financial Assistance (ERFA) Department for details.

faqs.question: How do I access my timetable and register for courses?
faqs.answer: Register for courses and view your class schedule on ZabDesk at zabdesk.szabist.edu.pk. Class schedules are also posted on notice boards. Registration is not allowed two weeks after classes begin, and students who are not registered cannot attend classes.

faqs.question: What are the class timings?
faqs.answer: Classes run six days a week in four slots: 8:15 AM to 11:15 AM, 11:30 AM to 2:30 PM, 2:45 PM to 5:45 PM, and 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Each course meets once a week for 3 hours with a 15-minute break. Timings may change during Ramadan.

faqs.question: How long is a semester?
faqs.answer: Fall and Spring semesters are 16 weeks long. Fall starts in August and Spring in January. The Summer semester starts in June and is a remedial semester where you can register for a maximum of 2 courses (6 credit hours).

faqs.question: How can I withdraw from a course?
faqs.answer: Submit a withdrawal request through ZabDesk's Online Course Withdrawal option before the 12th session. It must be approved by Academics, your Program Manager and the Records Department. You receive a 'W' grade, and the tuition amount is carried forward to the next semester rather than refunded.

faqs.question: What is the attendance policy?
faqs.answer: In each course you are allowed a maximum of 3 absences and 1 late arrival per semester. Beyond that limit you will be dropped from the course. A minimum of 80% attendance is also required to sit the final exam. There are no leaves at SZABIST, so manage your attendance carefully.

faqs.question: When are the mid-term and final exams?
faqs.answer: Mid-term exams are held in the 7th, 8th or 9th week of the semester and last 1.5 to 2 hours. The 16th week is a study week, and final exams are held in two weeks between the 17th and 19th week, lasting 2.5 hours. Exact dates are posted on ZabDesk and notice boards, and SMS alerts are sent to students.

faqs.question: How do I get my exam admit card?
faqs.answer: Print a colour copy of your admit card from ZabDesk with a recent picture and get it verified and stamped by the Examination Department with your valid SZABIST ID card. You must bring the verified admit card to every final exam. A duplicate admit card costs Rs 1,000.

faqs.question: What if I miss an exam?
faqs.answer: A retake (deferral) is possible only with documents such as a specialist medical certificate, death certificate for immediate family, Hajj documents, or approval for force majeure, and with permission of your Program Manager and HoD. Apply within two weeks after the exam week. A separate retake exam costs Rs 5,000.

faqs.question: How does grading work at SZABIST?
faqs.answer: Grades run from A+ (90-100, 4.00 points) down to C- (55-59, 1.50 points); below 55 is an F. Undergraduate degrees need a CGPA of at least 2.00 to graduate. If you retake a course, the better grade is counted. There are no grace marks.

faqs.question: What is academic probation?
faqs.answer: If your CGPA falls below the required minimum you are placed on First Probation, then Second Probation, and dismissed if it is not improved. The minimum CGPA is 1.75 for undergraduate, 2.25 for Masters, 2.50 for MS and 2.75 for PhD programs. Summer semesters do not count towards probation.

faqs.question: Can I get my paper rechecked or challenge a grade?
faqs.answer: Yes. For final exam papers you can fill the scrutiny form for recounting or re-checking, pay the fee and submit it to the Examination Department. If your claim is correct the fee is refunded. For any grade discrepancy, submit an objection within 5 working days of the tentative results on ZabDesk.

faqs.question: Where is the library and what are its timings?
faqs.answer: The main library is on the Third Floor of the State Life Building, ext. 126. It is open Monday to Saturday from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, closed on Sunday, with a break on Friday from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM. Students also get access to the HEC Digital Library inside campus.

faqs.question: How do I borrow a book and what are the library fines?
faqs.answer: Get a library membership card first. You can borrow two books at a time for three days. A late return fine is Rs 50 per day per book. If a book is damaged you pay its full price, and if lost you pay 200% of its price or replace it with a new copy. Reference books, journals and newspapers cannot be borrowed.

faqs.question: Where can I do group study?
faqs.answer: Group discussions are not allowed in the library, so use the study rooms on the Fourth Floor. Eating and drinking are not allowed in the library, classrooms, labs and study rooms.

faqs.question: What computer labs and IT facilities are available?
faqs.answer: SZABIST Hyderabad has computing, software, FYP, AI, networking and general labs, plus Wi-Fi on campus. Labs are open Monday to Saturday from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with colour and laser printing at nominal cost. You may not install your own software on lab computers without written approval.

faqs.question: How do I join a student society?
faqs.answer: SZABIST has many societies under the SZABIST Student Council (SSC), including the Oratory, Performing Arts, Sports, Welfare, ACM, IEEE, AWS, Google DSC and MLSA societies, and AIESEC. Visit the SSC Office on the Eighth Floor (Room 76) or the Student Advisor to find out how to join.

faqs.question: How do I start a new society or organize an event?
faqs.answer: Student societies and associations are registered with the Office of Student Advisory. Event and project ideas need a written proposal with scope, purpose and financials, approved by your Program Manager and Head of Department. Contact the Student Advisor or the SSC Office to begin.

faqs.question: How can I contact SZABIST Hyderabad?

Office hours are Monday to Friday 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Saturday 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, and closed on Sunday. Individual offices may have different timings.

faqs.question: What is the university phone number and extensions?
faqs.answer: The main number is (92-22) 2782442-3 and 2730027-8. Extensions: Admissions 106, Academics 139, Records 153, Finance 154, Examination 111, Library 126, IT/Network 130, Student Career Services 148.

faqs.question: What are the email addresses of the main offices?
faqs.answer: General: info@hyd.szabist.edu.pk. Admissions: info.admissions@hyd.szabist.edu.pk. Head of Campus: hoc@hyd.szabist.edu.pk. Campus Counsellor: campus.counsellor@hyd.szabist.edu.pk. Student Disciplinary Committee: sdc@szabist.edu.pk.

faqs.question: Where is SZABIST Hyderabad located?
faqs.answer: The campus is in the State Life Building, Thandi Sarak, Hyderabad, Sindh, Pakistan, and uses the Ground, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 8th floors. It is accessible by public transport and private vehicles, with parking available and wheelchair access.

faqs.question: Who is the Head of Campus?
faqs.answer: The Head of Campus at SZABIST Hyderabad is Mr. Jawad Raza Khoso, Assistant Professor. His office is on the Fourth Floor, and you can email hoc@hyd.szabist.edu.pk.

faqs.question: How do I access ZabDesk and what if I forget my password?
faqs.answer: ZabDesk is the student portal at zabdesk.szabist.edu.pk where you register for courses, check grades and fee status. You get a user ID and password at registration. If you forget your password, contact the Network Operation Centre (IT Help) on the Fourth Floor, ext. 130, Monday to Friday 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

faqs.question: How do I get a student ID card?
faqs.answer: As soon as you receive your registration number, send a student ID card request through ZabDesk. Your valid SZABIST ID card is required for exams and library membership.

faqs.question: Is there a cafeteria and what other facilities are on campus?
faqs.answer: Yes. The cafeteria is on the Third Floor (Room 44). Other facilities include a photocopy shop, activity rooms, an indoor games area on the Eighth Floor, a seminar hall, study rooms and a Wellness Centre. The campus must be vacated by 10:00 PM.

faqs.question: Is hostel or on-campus housing available?
faqs.answer: The SZABIST Hyderabad student handbook does not list hostel or on-campus housing. Please contact the Admission Office on the Ground Floor, ext. 106, to confirm current accommodation options.

faqs.question: Is counseling or a wellness centre available?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Wellness Centre is on the Eighth Floor (Room 64) and SZABIST has an in-house campus psychologist and counselor. You can email campus.counsellor@hyd.szabist.edu.pk directly or ask your Program Manager to refer you. Academic and career counseling are also available.

faqs.question: How do I get a transcript or other documents?
faqs.answer: Apply through the Records Office on the Ground Floor (ext. 153, Monday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM). Provisional transcripts are issued after paying the applicable fee and submitting the request form. The final transcript and degree are issued only after degree clearance and clearing all dues. Duplicate or revised transcripts take at least one month, and an urgent duplicate degree takes two working weeks.

faqs.question: Who is my academic advisor or Program Manager?
faqs.answer: Your Program Manager (PM) is your first point of contact for academic matters like course selection, attendance and registration. Each department has its own PM, so ask me for your program, for example the PM of BSCS, BSSE, BBA, MBA, BSSS, BS Accounting and Finance, or MS/PhD. The Student Advisor is Ms. Aisha Iqbal Shaikh (aisha.iqbal@hyd.szabist.edu.pk).

faqs.question: Can I transfer credits from another university?
faqs.answer: Yes, credits from HEC-recognized institutions can be transferred if the course content is similar and you scored at least grade B or 80% (MS and PhD have separate rules). A maximum of 50% of degree credits can be transferred. Fill the Course Transfer form at reception in consultation with your Program Manager and submit it to the Admission Office.

faqs.question: Is there a career services office and internship support?
faqs.answer: Yes. Student Career Services and Alumni Relations is on the Eighth Floor (ext. 148). It arranges career fairs, recruitment drives, mock interviews, workshops and internship placements. Undergraduate students must complete a graded 3-credit-hour internship or field experience.

faqs.question: What is the dress code and code of conduct?
faqs.answer: Students must wear suitable attire. Flip-flops, slides, loungewear, shorts, three-quarter trousers and ripped jeans are not allowed, and formal wear is expected for special occasions. Smoking, drugs, alcohol, harassment and misuse of property are strictly prohibited, and disciplinary action may follow.

faqs.question: What is the plagiarism policy?
faqs.answer: SZABIST has zero tolerance for plagiarism, and a plagiarised course gets an F grade. Turnitin is used to check theses and research reports, and the overall similarity index must be below 20%, with any single source under 5%.

faqs.question: What are the convocation, gold medal and honors roll criteria?
faqs.answer: Apply for online final transcript clearance through ZabDesk to be eligible for convocation. Gold and Silver Medals go to the top two CGPAs in a graduating batch with a minimum CGPA of 3.20. Graduating students with a CGPA of 3.50 or higher are placed on the Chancellor's Honors Roll.

faqs.question: How long do I have to complete my degree?
faqs.answer: The maximum time allowed from admission is 6 years for undergraduate, 4 years for Masters and MS, and 8 years for PhD programs. Required minimum CGPA at completion is 2.00 for undergraduate, 2.50 for Masters, 2.75 for MS and 3.00 for PhD.
